name: New Relic
description: Protects against destructive New Relic CLI/API operations like deleting entities \ or alerting resources.

destructive_patterns.name: newrelic-entity-delete
destructive_patterns.description: newrelic entity delete removes a New Relic entity, impacting observability.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting a New Relic entity removes all associated telemetry data, relationships, \ and alert configurations. Historical metrics for this entity will no longer be \ accessible.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - newrelic entity search: Find and verify the entity first \ - Tag the entity as deprecated instead of deleting \ - Export entity configuration before deletion

destructive_patterns.name: newrelic-apm-app-delete
destructive_patterns.description: newrelic apm application delete removes an APM application.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting an APM application removes all application performance data, traces, \ and associated alert policies. You lose visibility into application behavior \ and historical performance trends.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - newrelic apm application get <id>: Review application details first \ - Disable the APM agent in your application instead \ - Export application settings and dashboards as backup

destructive_patterns.name: newrelic-workload-delete
destructive_patterns.description: newrelic workload delete removes a workload definition.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting a workload removes the logical grouping of entities and any associated \ health status calculations. Teams using this workload for service overview will \ lose their aggregated view.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - Review workload entities and dependencies first \ - Export workload definition using the API \ - Modify the workload rather than deleting and recreating

destructive_patterns.name: newrelic-synthetics-delete
destructive_patterns.description: newrelic synthetics delete removes a synthetics monitor.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting a synthetics monitor stops all uptime and availability checking for \ the monitored endpoint. You will no longer receive alerts when the endpoint \ becomes unavailable or slow.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - Disable the monitor temporarily instead of deleting \ - Export monitor configuration as code (Terraform/Pulumi) \ - newrelic synthetics search: Verify you're deleting the correct monitor

destructive_patterns.name: newrelic-api-delete
destructive_patterns.description: New Relic API DELETE calls remove monitoring/alerting resources.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Direct API DELETE calls permanently remove New Relic resources without \ confirmation. Alert policies, dashboards, and monitors are deleted immediately.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - GET the resource first to verify the ID and export configuration \ - Use the New Relic CLI for better feedback and confirmation \ - Use Terraform/Pulumi for version-controlled resource management

destructive_patterns.name: newrelic-graphql-delete-mutation
destructive_patterns.description: New Relic GraphQL delete mutations can remove monitoring resources.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
GraphQL delete mutations remove New Relic resources via the NerdGraph API. \ This affects entities, dashboards, alert policies, and other observability \ resources.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - Run a query first to verify the GUID or resource ID \ - Use the New Relic CLI or UI for deletion with better feedback \ - Export the resource definition before deletion
